sources.title: CVE-2005-2148: NVD vulnerability record
sources.snippet: Cacti 0.8.6e and earlier does not perform proper input validation to protect against common attacks, which allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary commands or SQL by sending a legitimate value in a POST request or cookie, then specifying the attack string in the URL, which causes the get_request_var function to return the wrong value in the $_REQUEST variable, which is cleansed while the original malicious $_GET value remains unmodified, as demonstrated in (1) graph_image.php and (2) graph.php.
supports: NVD lists CVE-2005-2148 for a product matching 'Cacti'; version applicability and exploitation are unverified.

sources.title: CVE-2025-24367: Cacti Graph Template RCE Vulnerability
sources.snippet: UNTRUSTED WEB RESEARCH (not PCAP evidence). CVE-2025-24367 is a remote code execution vulnerability in Cacti. Learn about its impact, affected versions, and mitigation methods. | Webpage excerpt: [PARTIAL WEBPAGE: only first 150000 bytes examined] Vulnerability Database/CVE-2025-24367 CVE-2025-24367: Cacti Graph Template RCE Vulnerability CVE-2025-24367 is a remote code execution vulnerability in Cacti that allows authenticated users to create malicious PHP scripts via graph templates. This article covers technical details, affected versions, and patches. CVE-2025-24367 is a critical Remote Code Execution (RCE) vulnerability affecting Cacti, an open source performance and fault management framework widely used for network monitoring and graphing. An authenticated Cacti user can abuse the graph creation and graph template functionality to create arbitrary PHP scripts in the web root of the application, leading to remote code execution on the server. This vulnerability allows attackers with valid credentials to leverage the graph template system to write malicious PHP files directly into the web-accessible directory structure. Once these files are created, they can be accessed via HTTP requests, resulting in arbitrary code execution with the privileges of the web server process. Authenticated attackers can achieve full server compromise through arbitrary PHP file creation in the web root, enabling complete control over the Cacti server and potentially the broader network infrastructure it monitors. Cacti versions prior to 1.2.29

sources.title: CVE-2026-39893 – Pre-Auth SQL Injection – Cacti 1.2.30 ...
sources.snippet: UNTRUSTED WEB RESEARCH (not PCAP evidence). CVE-2026-39893 is a critical pre-authentication SQL injection vulnerability in Cacti, an open source performance and fault management ... | Webpage excerpt: [PARTIAL WEBPAGE: only first 150000 bytes examined] CVE-2026-39893 – Pre-Auth SQL Injection – Cacti 1.2.30 and prior CVE-2026-39893 is a critical pre-authentication SQL injection vulnerability in Cacti, an open source performance and fault management framework, affecting all versions up to and including 1.2.30. The flaw resides in graph_view.php, where the rfilter request variable is concatenated directly into an SQL RLIKE clause without sanitization, and is reachable without credentials on any Cacti deployment with guest graph vie Root cause: The rfilter parameter passed to graph_view.php (at lines 470 and 753) is directly concatenated into an SQL RLIKE clause with no input sanitization or parameterized query handling, constituting an improper neutralization of special elements in an SQL command (CWE-89). Trigger conditions: Exploitation requires no authentication. Cacti’s graph viewing endpoint supports unauthenticated guest access via the configured guest user account — a configuration present on many internet-facing Cacti deployments. Impact: Successful exploitation grants an attacker full read access to the underlying database, the ability to modify or corrupt database records, and the potential to cause service disruption through resource exhaustion. CVSS impact metrics are rated High across confidentiality, integrity, and availability (C:H/I:H/A:H). Cacti versions 1.2.30 and prior (all versions up to and including 1.2.30)
